<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask examples-docs`; do not edit. -->

`fauxfield init my-shop --example ecommerce` writes a realistic Workspace with one Server per microservice, deterministic data (every Server sets `fake_seed`), a `local` and a `staging` Environment and a `docs/README.md`. `fauxfield init --list-examples` prints the list; the app offers the same choices on the Welcome view and in the Command Palette (*Workspace: New from Example…*). Existing files are never changed. Two examples are not meant to run together: they share the 4001+ port block.

```bash
fauxfield init my-shop --example ecommerce
fauxfield validate -w my-shop
fauxfield run my-shop
```

| Example | Title | Servers | Routes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ecommerce` | E-commerce platform | 6 | 44 |
| `banking` | Fintech and banking | 6 | 49 |
| `social` | Social network | 6 | 50 |
| `food-delivery` | Food delivery | 6 | 48 |
| `ride-hailing` | Ride-hailing platform | 6 | 49 |
| `saas-billing` | Multi-tenant SaaS billing | 6 | 49 |
| `healthcare` | Health records (synthetic) | 6 | 48 |
| `iot-fleet` | IoT fleet management | 6 | 53 |
| `streaming-media` | Streaming media service | 6 | 54 |
| `travel-booking` | Travel booking | 6 | 51 |

## E-commerce platform

`fauxfield init <path> --example ecommerce`

Six microservices of an online shop: browse the catalog, fill a cart, place an order, pay (the payments Server fires a webhook Callback to the orders Server), ship and manage users.

```text
catalog          :4001  8 Routes
cart             :4002  7 Routes
orders           :4003  8 Routes
payments         :4004  7 Routes
shipping         :4005  7 Routes
users            :4006  7 Routes
```

List products:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4001/products
```

Charge a card (watch the webhook Callback in Traffic):

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4004/charges -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"amount":4999,"card":"4242424242424242"}'
```

A declined card returns 402:

```bash
curl -si -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4004/charges -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"amount":4999,"card":"4000000000000002"}'
```

## Fintech and banking

`fauxfield init <path> --example banking`

Six services of a demo bank: accounts and holders, a paginated transactions ledger, transfers that reject insufficient funds with a 422, card freeze controls, a KYC status workflow and FX rates.

```text
accounts         :4001  9 Routes
transactions     :4002  8 Routes
transfers        :4003  8 Routes
cards            :4004  8 Routes
kyc              :4005  8 Routes
fx               :4006  8 Routes
```

List accounts:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4001/accounts
```

Create a transfer:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4003/transfers -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"amount":250}'
```

An oversized transfer returns 422 insufficient funds:

```bash
curl -si -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4003/transfers -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"amount":50000}'
```

## Social network

`fauxfield init <path> --example social`

Six services of a social app: profiles, posts with likes, comments, a paginated and cursor-based feed, a WebSocket notification stream and a media upload stub that answers 413 for oversized files.

```text
profiles         :4001  8 Routes
posts            :4002  9 Routes
comments         :4003  8 Routes
feed             :4004  9 Routes
notifications    :4005  8 Routes
media            :4006  8 Routes
```

List posts:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4002/posts
```

Read the paginated feed:

```bash
curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:4004/feed?page=2'
```

An oversized upload returns 413:

```bash
curl -si -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4006/uploads -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"filename":"clip.mp4","bytes":50000000}'
```

## Food delivery

`fauxfield init <path> --example food-delivery`

Six services of a delivery app: restaurants, menus, orders, couriers (poll their location), a WebSocket tracking stream that pushes courier positions, and promotions with redeemable codes.

```text
restaurants      :4001  8 Routes
menus            :4002  8 Routes
orders           :4003  8 Routes
couriers         :4004  8 Routes
tracking         :4005  8 Routes
promotions       :4006  8 Routes
```

List restaurants:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4001/restaurants
```

Place an order:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4003/orders/place -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"items":[1,2],"total":24.5,"restaurant_id":3}'
```

A closed restaurant returns 409:

```bash
curl -si -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4003/orders/place -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"items":[1],"restaurant_id":13}'
```

## Ride-hailing platform

`fauxfield init <path> --example ride-hailing`

A ride-hailing backend: riders request trips, drivers go online and accept, the trips Server enforces a state machine (requested, accepted, arrived, in progress, completed), pricing applies a surge multiplier from a Server Variable, payments charge the fare and ratings close the loop.

```text
riders           :4001  7 Routes
drivers          :4002  9 Routes
trips            :4003  9 Routes
pricing          :4004  8 Routes
payments         :4005  8 Routes
ratings          :4006  8 Routes
```

Fare estimate with surge (edit the surge Variable on the pricing Server):

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4004/estimate -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"pickup":"Central Station"}'
```

Request a trip:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4003/trips/request -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"pickup":"Central Station"}'
```

Completing an already completed trip returns 409:

```bash
curl -si -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4003/trips/3/complete
```

## Multi-tenant SaaS billing

`fauxfield init <path> --example saas-billing`

A multi-tenant SaaS backend: OAuth2 token and refresh with 401 and 403 rules, tenants and members, subscriptions, invoices, metered usage, and a webhooks Server whose Callbacks retry up to three times against a sibling Server.

```text
auth             :4001  9 Routes
tenants          :4002  8 Routes
subscriptions    :4003  8 Routes
invoices         :4004  8 Routes
usage            :4005  8 Routes
webhooks         :4006  8 Routes
```

Get an OAuth2 token:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4001/oauth/token -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"grant_type":"client_credentials","client_secret":"demo"}'
```

Start a subscription (fires a webhook Callback with 3 retries):

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4003/subscriptions/start -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"plan":"team"}'
```

Admin route without a role returns 403:

```bash
curl -si http://127.0.0.1:4001/admin/users -H 'authorization: Bearer demo' -H 'x-role: member'
```

## Health records (synthetic)

`fauxfield init <path> --example healthcare`

A synthetic health-records backend: patients, appointments, prescriptions, labs, insurance eligibility and providers. All people, drugs and identifiers are made up; nothing here is real patient data.

```text
patients         :4001  8 Routes
appointments     :4002  8 Routes
prescriptions    :4003  8 Routes
labs             :4004  8 Routes
insurance        :4005  8 Routes
providers        :4006  8 Routes
```

List synthetic patients:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4001/patients
```

Check insurance eligibility:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4005/eligibility -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"member_id":"M-1001"}'
```

A lapsed member is not eligible:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4005/eligibility -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"member_id":"LAPSED-7"}'
```

## IoT fleet management

`fauxfield init <path> --example iot-fleet`

A fleet of connected devices: manage devices, ingest and read telemetry, roll out firmware, raise alerts, track geofences and watch a live WebSocket stream of readings.

```text
devices          :4001  9 Routes
telemetry        :4002  9 Routes
firmware         :4003  9 Routes
alerts           :4004  9 Routes
geofences        :4005  9 Routes
stream           :4006  8 Routes
```

List devices:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4001/devices
```

Send a command to a device:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4001/devices/7/command -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"command":"reboot"}'
```

Latest time series (a points value above 500 returns 400):

```bash
curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:4002/telemetry/7/series?points=24'
```

## Streaming media service

`fauxfield init <path> --example streaming-media`

A video and music streaming backend: browse the catalog, fetch a playback manifest and static media segments, manage playlists, get recommendations, handle subscriptions and collect analytics.

```text
catalog          :4001  9 Routes
playback         :4002  10 Routes
playlists        :4003  9 Routes
recommendations  :4004  8 Routes
subscriptions    :4005  9 Routes
analytics        :4006  9 Routes
```

Search the catalog:

```bash
curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:4001/search?q=harbor'
```

Fetch a playback manifest:

```bash
curl -si http://127.0.0.1:4002/manifest/12
```

Fetch a static media segment:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4002/media/segment1.txt
```

## Travel booking

`fauxfield init <path> --example travel-booking`

A travel agency backend: search flights, hotels and cars, hold then confirm or cancel a booking, pay (the payments Server fires a webhook Callback to the bookings Server) and earn loyalty points.

```text
flights          :4001  9 Routes
hotels           :4002  9 Routes
cars             :4003  8 Routes
bookings         :4004  9 Routes
payments         :4005  8 Routes
loyalty          :4006  8 Routes
```

Search flights:

```bash
curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:4001/flights/search?from=BER&to=AMS'
```

Hold a booking:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4004/bookings/hold -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"item":"flight"}'
```

Pay (watch the webhook Callback in Traffic); the card 4000000000000002 returns 402:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4005/payments -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"amount":24900,"card":"4242424242424242"}'
```
